description.narrative: The development objective of the Cusco Regional Development Project for Peru is to improve the quality of tourism and solid waste management services and increase the resilience of the tourism sector to the impacts of natural disasters in the provinces of Calca, Urubamba, and Cusco. The project has four components. The first component is development and consolidation of tourism services. The objective of this component is to improve the quality and coverage of tourism services in the sacred valley and surrounding areas. The second component is integrated solid waste management. This component aims at improving the local capacity to clean streets and public places and to efficiently collect, transport, and dispose of solid waste in the provinces of Calca, Urubamba, and Cusco. The third component is disaster risk management and disaster preparedness. The objective of this component is to increase the resilience of the local population, tourists, and infrastructure in touristic areas with high vulnerability to natural disasters. The component is aimed at increasing the resilience of the local population and tourism infrastructure to natural disasters. The fourth component is institutional strengthening, management and monitoring, and evaluation. This component will support the capacity building of the principal institutions involved in the operation of tourism activities in the sacred valley, and commission to supervise the cultural tourism plan PERU-UNESCO- Comision Especial para Supervigilar el Plan Turistico Cultural PERUUNESCO (COPESCO), including its project coordination unit (PCU). The component will strengthen the institutional capacity of the PCU, special regional project of plan COPESCO- Proyecto Especial Regional (PER plan) COPESCO, to enhance the institutional capabilities required for the successful implementation of project activities, including compliance with procurement, safeguards, financial management, and monitoring and evaluation requirements.

To improve the quality of tourism and solid waste management services and increase the resilience of the tourism sector to the impacts of natural disasters in the provinces of Calca, Urubamba, and Cusco.

title.narrative: Number of people (tourists and residents) covered by a functioning early warning system for natural disasters under the Project

comment.narrative: Technical specifications for the early warning systems were completed. However, none of the originally planned early warning systems was implemented. In the August 2017 restructuring, the early warning systems of Vilcanota and Ccochoq were withdrawn. In the January 8 2019 restructuring, the implementation of the early warning systems of Kitamayu and Patacancha were dropped.

title.narrative: Percent reduction in the dissatisfaction rating of the upgraded tourism sites under the Project

comment.narrative: The baseline survey to measure this indicator was not carried out. Although technical specifications were completed, the works at archeological sites and miradores were not executed. Therefore, changes in tourism satisfaction cannot be attributed to the project. The indicator was deleted in the January 8 2019 restructuring.

title.narrative: Existing tourism sites equipped with improved infrastructure installments

comment.narrative: The technical designs for the Ollantaytambo and Miradores subcomponents were finalized. The contract for the preparation of the technical design for the Pisac works is being subject to arbitration. None of the works and improvements were executed.

title.narrative: Informal and formalized recyclers (households) benefiting from Project social inclusion activities.

comment.narrative: After closing date, the implementation of the social inclusion plan for the Urubamba waste pickers was completed. It included updating the registry of 18 waste pickers throughout the province, their training, and the formation of segregator associations. Likewise, segregators were included in the municipalities' waste management processes. The implementation of the social inclusion plan was completed in July 2019.

title.narrative: Number of municipalities provided with equipment and works for improved collection, recycling and street sweeping

comment.narrative: Three municipalities in Urubamba and four municipalities in Calca received equipment for improved collection, recycling and street sweeping.

title.narrative: Industrial and municipal waste disposal capacity created under the project

comment.narrative: The Urubamba landfill (25 metric tons) was completed. Both the Cusco (350 metric tons) and Calca (15 metric tons) landfills were dropped from the Project.

title.narrative: Number of people (tourists and residents) in the Project area from whom waste is collected and disposed in one of the Project sanitary landfills

comment.narrative: The Urubamba landfill was completed during the project. However, the landfill was not operational by project closing date. Activities to ensure its adequate and sustainable operation were ongoing, paid with government funds, in October 2019.The Cusco and Calca landfills were dropped.
The lack of completion of most project activities and works meant that the projected population did not benefit from the project by closing date.

title.narrative: Emergency Preparedness Plan established for tourists

comment.narrative: This indicator was deleted in the January 8 2019 restructuring. Terms of reference were prepared for the preparation of the Plan.

title.narrative: Strategic Regional Plan updated for prevention and reduction of disaster risk

comment.narrative: The strategic regional plan was updated.

title.narrative: Pilot Competitive Fund for Tourism for small businesses in the Sacred Valley operational

comment.narrative: The pilot competitive fund was launched and partially executed. 50 small enterprises were registered. However, misprocurement was declared over this contract and activities were not completed by closing date.

title.narrative: Number of Provincial sanitary landfills constructed under the Project

comment.narrative: The Urubamba landfill was completed, while the Cusco and Calca landfills were dropped in the August 2017 and January 8 2019 restructurings respectively.
